component_findings.abstraction_ceremony: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Reusable abstractions such as types, interfaces/traits/generics or equivalent mechanisms can be declared and consumed without excessive scaffolding. Evidence basis: Inspected reusable comparison-language Python micro-benchmark programs (mb00-mb11) and adversarial programs under the assigned readable paths. Measured source line counts, syntactic density, and idiomatic construct usage relative to logic expressed. | mb04.py (FP arithmetic): 72 lines total; core workload() function is about 20 lines expressing nested loop over M=4000, R=75000 with 4 accumulators and comprehension-based array initialization. | mb07.py (merge sort): 104 lines total; msort() core algorithm implemented in about 35 lines using ping-pong buffer swap idiom (src, dst = dst, src), concise and idiomatic. | List/array comprehensions collapse multi-line init loops into single expressions. | Dynamic typing reduces declaration tokens, but pinned array('d')/array('q') containers and ban on vectorized/library-accelerated computation force explicit index loops for hot paths, adding lines versus idiomatic high-level Python with numpy. | No numpy/vectorization observed or permitted per the frozen binding table, equalizing conciseness comparisons across languages. | Adversarial programs (ADV-01..ADV-26) are uniformly very short (93-440 bytes), minimal single-purpose snippets with no incidental boilerplate.

metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic mandatory ceremony for the same kinds of ordinary programs. Do not reuse raw LOC/bytes/tokens as the score and do not reward external libraries.

component_findings.consistency_regular_forms: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Similar concepts use regular forms with few special-case spellings or context-dependent surface rules. Evidence basis: Assessed naming, structure, docstrings, and control-flow clarity of the same reusable Python micro-benchmark and adversarial source files. | Every micro-benchmark file begins with a clear module docstring naming the workload, citing the frozen spec section, and stating forbidden shortcuts, aiding comprehension of intent versus implementation. | Helper class Lehmer (Park-Miller LCG) is small, uses __slots__, and has self-documenting method names (next_int, next_unit) repeated consistently across files. | Control flow uses plain while/for loops with descriptive local variable names (lo, mid, hi, i, j, k in mb07; s1..s4 accumulators in mb04) mirroring textbook algorithm descriptions. | CLI harness (main()) is identical in structure across files, reducing cognitive load across the corpus. | Significant whitespace and lack of braces/semicolons keep visual noise low; comments annotate non-obvious pinned-requirement constraints at point of relevance. | Minor cost: manual loop-increment style instead of augmented assignment/enumerate in some hot loops, adopted for cross-language performance comparability rather than idiomatic Python.
